segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Brazil · Yemen · Jobs
bullets: Weak jobs report, yields still high

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Monday, October fifth.
Today: Brazil's first round ends in a surprise and a runoff, Yemen's government launches an offensive, and a weak jobs report meets very high borrowing costs.
Plus a new Supreme Court term, two Pacific hurricanes, and a playoff series that is tied. Let's go.

Brazil's first round is done. NPR reports Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has about forty-seven percent, and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva about forty-five, with more than ninety-nine percent of votes counted.
Polls had Lula ahead, so this was a surprise. Neither man cleared fifty percent, so they meet in a runoff on October twenty-fifth.

segments.strap: YEMEN OFFENSIVE; HOUTHIS CLAIM ARAMCO STRIKES; HORMUZ STAYS SHUT
segments.headline: The Gulf and Yemen

graphic.title: Yemen and the Gulf
bullets: Houthis claim missile and drone strikes on Aramco
Iran: Hormuz shut until its conditions are met

lines.text: The A.P. reports Yemen's internationally recognized government has begun a coastal offensive against the Houthis, backed by a Saudi-led air campaign. The coalition says one hundred fighter jets are supporting it. The A.P. says those details are not independently verified.
Reuters reports the Houthis say they fired missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed that. It is a claim.

Iran repeats that the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until its seven conditions are met. Separately, Israel's defense minister ordered a general closure of the West Bank and Gaza for today and for October seventh.

segments.strap: BRENT ~$102; G7 TO RELEASE 100 MILLION BARRELS
segments.headline: Oil and the G7

graphic.title: Oil on Monday
bullets: Reuters: G7 agreed Friday to release crude and diesel
Middle East exports above pre-war levels on 4 of last 7 September days

lines.text: Reuters has Brent at one hundred two dollars and thirty cents this morning, and U.S. crude at ninety dollars and sixty-two cents.

The report cites a Friday agreement by the G7 to release one hundred million barrels of crude and diesel. It also cites shipping data showing Middle East exports above pre-war levels on four of the last seven days of September. Quotes vary by tracker. One had Brent near one hundred one.
The economy added twenty-nine thousand jobs in September. Economists expected about eighty-four thousand. Unemployment rose to four point two percent, from an expected four point one.

Fed funds futures now put the odds of no October move at about seventy-two percent. The ten-year yield is near five point one eight, after touching five point three four four on Thursday, the highest since two thousand two.

Bitcoin is near eighty-six thousand dollars, which CoinDesk ties to the weaker jobs data. Today at ten a.m. Eastern, the September services report is due from the Institute for Supply Management. Japan's Nikkei gained two point four percent to nearly seventy thousand.

segments.strap: TRUMP ANNOUNCES FEDERAL A.I. 'SUPER INTELLIGENCE FORCE'
segments.headline: A.I. news

graphic.title: A.I. and Washington
bullets: SpaceX A.I. unit to be renamed SpaceXSI (Musk)

lines.text: The A.P. reports President Trump announced a federal Super Intelligence Force, led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, to coordinate federal A.I. efforts and engage outside groups.

Reuters reports Elon Musk says SpaceX will rename its A.I. unit from SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI. No timing was given. And Axios reports Nvidia-backed Reflection is preparing an open-weight model, with no release date.

segments.strap: SUPREME COURT TERM OPENS; CLIMATE-LIABILITY CASE ARGUED
segments.headline: The Court returns

graphic.title: A new Supreme Court term
bullets: Suncor v. Boulder County argued today
A test of climate-damage suits against energy firms (A.P.)
Congress in recess until after Nov. 3

lines.text: The Supreme Court's new term opens today. First up, at ten a.m., is Suncor Energy versus Boulder County. The A.P. calls it a test of climate-damage lawsuits against energy companies.

This is an argument, not a ruling. A decision comes later. Meanwhile Congress is in recess until after the November third election, and Trump is on the campaign trail. A generic-ballot average has Democrats ahead by five point nine.

segments.strap: U.S. MEASLES: 3,887 CASES, MOST IN 35 YEARS
segments.headline: Measles count

lines.text: The C.D.C. counts three thousand eight hundred eighty-seven confirmed U.S. measles cases as of October first. That is up two hundred twenty-eight in a week, and the most in thirty-five years.
Forty-seven jurisdictions have cases. About ninety-five percent are linked to outbreaks, and about ninety-three percent involve people who were unvaccinated or whose status is unknown.

segments.strap: HURRICANES RACHEL, NOLO; CALIF. HEAT; SOUTHEAST RAIN
segments.headline: Storms and heat

graphic.title: Pacific hurricanes, Western heat
bullets: Rachel: no coastal watches; surf hazards for Baja
Nolo crossed the Date Line, moving west
California heat advisories to Oct. 8; easing Thursday
Flash-flood risk, Gulf Coast and Southeast

lines.text: Hurricane Rachel has ninety-mile-an-hour winds, moving west at eight, well off Baja. No coastal watches or warnings are in effect, but swells bring surf and rip-current hazards.
Japan's weather agency lists Nolo as a very strong typhoon with ninety-knot winds. The A.P. says it crossed the International Date Line over open water.

On land, California heat advisories run through October eighth, and the heat wave should begin weakening Thursday. A heavy-rain and flash-flood threat covers the central Gulf Coast and the Southeast through Friday.

segments.strap: BRAVES 3, DODGERS 2; BREWERS 4, PADRES 3; COLTS 30, COMMANDERS 13
segments.headline: Playoffs and football

graphic.title: Playoffs and Sunday football
bullets: ALDS Game 2: White Sox at Guardians, 5 p.m. ET
ALDS Game 2: Yankees at Rays, 8 p.m. ET

lines.text: Baseball. The Braves beat the Dodgers three to two in Game Two, so that series is tied. The Brewers beat the Padres four to three. Tonight, the White Sox are at the Guardians at five Eastern, and the Yankees are at the Rays at eight.

Football. The Colts beat the Commanders thirty to thirteen in London. Elsewhere: Patriots twenty-nine, Bills twenty-six. Rams twenty-four, Eagles twenty. Cowboys thirty-four, Texans thirty. Vikings and Forty-Niners remain unbeaten.
Injuries: Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase is out with a concussion. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left his game with an ankle injury. Tonight, Falcons at Packers, nine p.m.
In the W.N.B.A. semifinals, Atlanta beat New York ninety-two to eighty-two, and Golden State beat Las Vegas seventy-one to sixty.

graphic.title: Deals and weekend film
bullets: Warner film chiefs expected to leave; layoffs expected (A.P.)

lines.text: The A.P. reports Paramount Skydance expects to close its one hundred ten billion dollar purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday. Warner film executives Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy are expected to leave this week, with layoffs anticipated.

At the box office, the film Verity opened first with thirty-two point six million dollars. Digger took eight million. Those are estimates; final numbers are due today. And Avengers: Endgame Encore has passed Avatar in all-time worldwide gross, by a small margin.

segments.strap: DEBRIS FOUND OFF NANTUCKET IN AIR AMBULANCE SEARCH
segments.headline: Search off Massachusetts

lines.text: The A.P. reports the Coast Guard and partner crews have searched twenty-eight hundred forty square miles off Massachusetts for a medical flight carrying six people, missing between Bermuda and Boston. Debris was found off Nantucket. Sonar searches of the seabed are planned. No cause has been reported.
